top_strength: Dustin used the customer's move history to fast-track the quote instead of starting from scratch -- 'it looks like that previous move took a five person team about eight hours' -- and built genuine, unscripted rapport in the mechanical-keyboard exchange ('I like that mechanical keyboard man, I prefer those'), which kept a fairly thin call feeling personable.
coaching_note: You had a hot lead ask you directly 'do you guys have storage' and the answer was just 'no sir' -- that's the exact moment to route him to Ecobox or Sparefoot, and it was missed entirely. The rapport instinct is good -- now pair it with the full pricing and booking script so calls like this convert instead of ending in 'I'll send you an estimate.'
phone_presence_notes: Genuine warmth in the keyboard tangent and consistent affirmations ('Absolutely,' 'Yes sir,' 'Awesome man') kept Charlie comfortable and responsive, even though the call itself covered very little of the required content.
